From: Andy South <sout...@gmail.com>
Date: 10 February 2014 16:51
Subject: Re: CRAN package rworldmap

Hello Kjetil,

The issue with ylim & xlim has confused myself & others before.

The confusion occurs because R maximises what it can fit on a plot based on the limiting dimension, either X or Y. If the Y dimension is limiting then altering ylim will have no effect.

Have a look at the example below where fitting 3 world maps into a square should make the Y dimension the limiting one and you should see that ylim has an effect.

library(rworldmap)

x11()
oldpar <- par(mfrow=c(3, 1), mar=c(1, 0, 1, 0)) # b,l,t,r oma

mapCountryData()
mapCountryData(ylim=c(-70,70))
mapCountryData(ylim=c(-50,50))

par(oldpar)

Note also that there is a rworldmap group here where I post occasional questions & answers. You are welcome to join. Would you be happy for me to post this question & answer to the list ?

Happy mapping,

Andy
